text.p: The Zimbabwean government has stopped recruiting expatriate teachers following allegations of racism in recruiting at some private schools, Education Secretary Stanislous Chigwedere said on Sunday.

Chigwedere, a senior civil servant, said in a statement his ministry had received many complaints from local black teachers whose employment contracts had been "unfairly terminated" in favour of white expatriates.

He said his ministry felt there was some substance to the allegations as it had also noted that white teachers dominated most of the private schools when there were plenty of qualified blacks in the southern African country.

"We have taken note of this anomaly and I would like to... announce that the ministry will with immediate effect not approve applications for temporary employment for expatriate teachers. There will be no approval whatsoever," he said.

Zimbabwe has enjoyed relatively cordial race relations since it won independence from Britain in 1980 but over the past few years, black business pressure groups have been growing increasingly restive over what they say is a continuing dominance of the economy by minority whites.
Blacks outnumber whites 100-to-one in Zimbabwe, which has a population of 10.5 million.
